112: MISHNA: With regard to all [items] used as monetary value for another item - items for which it is typical to give money when acquiring. At this point, we assume that [the mishna] is discussing a coin: once [the seller] gains [the coin] he is obligated [to furnish] the item being exchanged for it -- if the coin is being given under the rubric of khalipin and not under the rubric of money -- in the way that we acquire by means of a scarf, and in the sense of [the verse] "a man drew off his shoe" (Ruth 4:7).

Once he acquires - [that is, once] the seller [acquires] it and pulls one zuz from the buyer under the rubric of khalipin acquisition, the buyer is responsible for any accidents that happen to the exchanged property, wherever they are -- whether they died or got lost -- [the buyer is still] required to pay [the rest of] the money which he agreed to give him. This is because when the seller pulls the scarf or the zuz under the rubric of khalipin, the goods are acquired by the buyer, wherever they may be.

If one exchanges an ox for a cow - once the owner of the cow [i.e., the buyer] pulls the ox, the cow is acquired by the buyer wherever it may be, and any accidents are his responsibility. The gemara will ask what is meant by [the term] "how so", since [it appeared as if the mishna] was coming to teach us that a coin could be used for khalipin exchange. Even though, if [the coin is given] under the rubric of money, we have established that money does not effect acquisition (Bava Metzia 44a), but only pulling of the goods does -- nevertheless, if he gives him [the coin] under the rubric of "scarf acquisition", the acquisition takes effect just as it would have with an actual scarf. Therefore, the mishna should have read: "how so? If one exchanges money for a cow."
